Read a moderated mixed graphical model at a value of the moderator

Source: R/mgm_moderated.R
condition.Rd

condition() reads a moderated mixed graphical model at one value of the moderator and returns that network as an ordinary psychnet; as.data.frame() and print() read the moderated fit itself. In a moderated network model, fitted by mgm_fit() with moderators, the strength of an edge between two variables can depend on the value of a third variable, the moderator, so each pairwise association has a main effect and an interaction with the moderator.

The network at a given moderator value, for example in a treatment group compared with a control group, or at low compared with high stress, shows how the conditional associations among the other variables differ across the moderator. For each pair, condition() takes the main effect plus the interaction evaluated at value, aggregated over the two nodewise regressions and combined by the AND or OR rule. Pairs whose main effect or interaction did not survive the rule at fitting time contribute nothing. The moderator itself carries no edges, and edge weights are magnitudes (non-negative), as in mgm::condition(). as.data.frame() on the moderated fit lists the size of the main effect and of the moderation effect of every pair with a nonzero effect, or, with value, the edges of the conditioned network.

value is read on the moderator's own scale: a level of a categorical moderator as coded in the data (1 or 2 for a moderator coded 1/2, "treat" for a factor level "treat"), or a raw value of a continuous moderator, so that value = mean(moderator) gives the network at the average moderator. The conditioned network is computed from the fit rather than estimated, so certificate() reports its certificate as missing.

condition() returns an undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet).

To fit the moderated model, use mgm_fit() with moderators.

Usage

condition(object, value, rule = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_moderated'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ..., value = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_moderated'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A psychnet_moderated fit from mgm_fit() with moderators.

value

A single moderator value: a level of a categorical moderator (number, label, factor or logical, as coded in the data), or a finite number on the raw scale of a continuous one. For as.data.frame(), NULL (default) gives the table of main and moderation effects.

rule

"AND" or "OR" combination of the two conditioned nodewise estimates of each pair. Default NULL uses the rule of the fit.

x

A psychnet_moderated fit.

row.names, optional

Ignored.

...

Unused.

Value

condition() returns an undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet); the value conditioned on is stored as mod_value.

as.data.frame() on the moderated fit returns, with value = NULL, one row per pair of nodes joined by a main effect or a moderation effect, with columns from, to, main_effect (magnitude of the pairwise main effect: the mean absolute nodewise estimate, zero when the pair does not survive the rule), interaction (magnitude of the moderator-by-pair interaction, NA for a pair that includes the moderator), moderated (interaction > 0, NA for a pair that includes the moderator) and involves_moderator. With a value, it returns the edge list (from, to, weight) of condition(x, value).

print() shows the number of nodes, the moderator and the fit settings, and returns x invisibly.

Functions

  • as.data.frame(psychnet_moderated): Main and moderation effects of every pair, or (with value) the edge list of the conditioned network.

  • print(psychnet_moderated): Print the nodes, the moderator and the fit settings.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when object is not a moderated fit, rule is not "AND" or "OR", or value is missing, not of length one, not a level of a categorical moderator, or not a finite number for a continuous one.

See also

mgm_fit() for fitting the moderated model; psychnet for the conditioned network.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x1 <- stats::rnorm(400); x2 <- stats::rnorm(400)
mod <- rep(1:2, each = 200)                 # moderator coded 1/2
y <- x1 * (mod == 2) + stats::rnorm(400)   # x1-y edge only when mod == 2
d <- data.frame(x1 = x1, x2 = x2, y = y, mod = mod)
fit <- mgm_fit(d, types = c("g", "g", "g", "c"), moderators = "mod")
fit
#> <psychnet_moderated> 4 nodes, moderator = mod
#>   gamma = 0.25, rule = AND, threshold = LW
#>   moderator levels: 1, 2
#>   as.data.frame(fit) for main and moderation effects; condition(fit, value) for the network at a moderator value.
as.data.frame(fit)            # main and moderation effects per edge
#>   from to main_effect interaction moderated involves_moderator
#> 1   x1  y           0   0.5665183      TRUE              FALSE
condition(fit, value = 1)     # no x1-y edge
#> <psychnet> mgm_moderated network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 0   (undirected)
condition(fit, value = 2)     # the x1-y edge appears
#> <psychnet> mgm_moderated network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 1   (undirected)
as.data.frame(fit, value = 2) # the same network as an edge list
#>   from to   weight
#> 1   x1  y 0.646064
